📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most important temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

Recent findings suggest that the Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

The east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess Athena from the head of her father Zeus, surrounded by the Olympian gods. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3.8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

But now there has been a breakthrough.

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

According to recent reports, brinkmann heads the Antiquities and Asia department at Frankfurt's Liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

The results are now on display in an exhibition at the Liebieghaus titled "Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle.".

Recent findings suggest that only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

It has been revealed that in 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the British Museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Industry observers note that then, in 2014, a visit to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!".

Nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in Rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

In a recent development, brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go.".

The researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3D scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

Digitally fitting the fragments together led to another crucial discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

The Romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment." This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Recent findings suggest that using a 3D printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7.7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most vital fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

Alongside works from the Liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the Vatican Museums and the Louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

It has been revealed that there is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

In the early 19th century, Elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

Greece, however, considers them stolen.

Recent findings suggest that for years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

Sources indicate that the exhibition "Athena, the Stage is Yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.
  • The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data showed with all ballots counted.
  • “We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo said in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.

The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data showed with all ballots counted.

“We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo said in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.

He will get the first chance at forming a coalition to obtain majority in parliament as Marin’s era as prime minister was expected to end.

Popular abroad, at home Marin faces battle to keep her job.

It has been revealed that “We have gained support, we have gained more seats (in parliament). That’s an excellent achievement, even if we did not finish first today,” the prime minister said in a speech to party members.

Marin, 37, the world’s youngest prime minister when she took office in 2019, is considered by fans around the globe as a millennial role model for progressive fresh leaders, but at home she has faced criticism for her partying and her government’s public spending.

Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin takes drug test following partying backlash.

While she remains very popular among many Finns, particularly young moderates, she antagonized some conservatives with lavish spending on pensions and education they see as not frugal enough.

The NCP has led in polls for almost two years although its lead had melted away in recent months. It has promised to curb spending and stop the rise of public debt, which has reached just over 70% of GDP since Marin took office in 2019.

Orpo accused Marin of eroding Finland’s economic resilience at a time when Europe’s energy crisis, driven by Russia’s war in Ukraine, has hit the country hard and the cost of living has increased.

Orpo has said he will negotiate with all groups to obtain a majority in parliament, while Marin has said her Social Democrats may govern with the NCP but will not go into government with the Finns Party.

Marin called the Finns Party “openly racist” during a debate in January – an accusation the nationalist group rejected.

The Finns Party’s main goal is to reduce what leader Riikka Purra has called “harmful” immigration from developing countries outside the European Union. It also calls for austerity policies to curb deficit spending, a stance it shares with the NCP.

Most notable of Marin’s foreign policy actions has been her push, along with President Sauli Niinisto, for the country to make a watershed policy U-turn by seeking NATO membership in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

That process is now almost complete, with Helsinki expected to join within days after all the Western defense alliance’s 30 members approved the accession.

Breaking: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism.
  • The findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal key differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
  • The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism. Although adults with and without autism demonstrated remarkably similar brain activity when researchers compared group averages, a closer examination uncovered striking differences between individuals. These differences were especially pronounced in brain regions involved in understanding and responding to social information.

The findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal key differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The discovery could help scientists better understand why autism varies so widely from person to person and eventually support more personalized approaches to care.

The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.

What Brain Scans Reveal When People Watch Movies.

According to recent reports, to explore these differences, the team examined previously collected brain imaging data from Indiana University and Caltech. The recordings captured brain activity as adults with and without autism watched movies from several genres, including animation, action, romantic comedy, and Hitchcockian thrillers.

Movies offered researchers a way to study how the brain responds to a constantly changing stream of sights, sounds, and social interactions. Unlike simple laboratory tasks, movies present a rich mixture of information that more closely resembles the complexity of everyday experiences.

Using the imaging data, the researchers trained a computational model to identify connections between brain activity and different elements of the movies. These included visual details, sounds, and more abstract social information, such as interactions between characters.

After training, the model was able to accurately predict activity across several brain systems.

Kliemann explained why this approach is particularly useful for investigating the social challenges sometimes associated with autism: "The computational model allowed us to look for robust brain responses to many different aspects of the complex, dynamic contexts in the movies.".

A Surprising Difference Hidden by Brain Activity Averages.

The most unexpected finding emerged when researchers compared the two groups.

Industry observers note that at first, the results suggested relatively little difference. When brain responses were averaged across participants, the model predicted activity in various brain systems similarly for adults with and without autism.

However, the picture changed when the researchers examined how much individual participants differed from others in their own group.

People with autism revealed substantially greater variation in their brain responses than participants without autism. In other words, although the overall group averages looked similar, the responses of individual autistic participants were much less alike.

This increased variability appeared across nearly every brain system examined. The strongest differences occurred in the social brain system, a network of regions involved in processing social information and understanding other people.

Why the Findings Could Change Autism Research.

The results raise notable questions about how scientists investigate autism. Many existing approaches to understanding and treating the condition rely heavily on comparing average measurements from groups of autistic and nonautistic individuals.

But if autistic people show considerable differences in how their brains process information, these averages may obscure some of the most meaningful findings.

Industry observers note that traer described the team's surprise: "We were surprised by the similarity of group averages. The results suggest that we need to focus on understanding the details of individual brain responses. How and why do they differ?".

Rather than searching only for brain activity patterns shared by everyone with autism, the findings point toward the potential value of studying individuals and identifying smaller groups with similar characteristics.

Kliemann highlighted what this could mean for future research and support: "Identifying ASD subgroups may help us build a more precise understanding of the condition and help develop ways to provide individually tailored support.".

The researchers now plan to investigate how these differences in brain activity relate to variations in autism-related behavior. They hope to determine where and when the differences emerge, how they are connected to individual characteristics, and what might explain them.

Ultimately, the findings suggest that understanding autism may require looking beyond the average brain and paying closer attention to the distinctive ways individuals process the world.

#35844. Breaking: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1183 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy.
  • In a recent development, researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words.
  • The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy. A new study from the University of Mississippi challenges the familiar image of psychopaths as cold and emotionless, revealing that their patterns of language can be far more complex than expected.

In a recent development, researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words. Some of the findings were particularly unexpected. For example, people who scored higher in meanness tended to use more positive language, while those with greater boldness used fewer words associated with anxiety.

The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.

Sources indicate that "The goal here is not to diagnose psychopathy based on language," said Ky Bray, an Ole Miss doctoral candidate in psychology. "It's to point to the fact that psychopathy reveals up in everyday behaviors, even subtle behaviors like language.

"If we want to understand psychopathy and the different traits that comprise it, we need to think creatively about how these traits shape social interaction.".

What 450 Life Stories Revealed About Psychopathy.

The researchers used a psychological framework known as the Triarchic Model of Psychopathy, which examines three distinct personality dimensions. Boldness generally involves confidence and fearlessness, meanness reflects tendencies toward callousness and reduced empathy, and disinhibition involves difficulties with impulse control. According to Laura Drislane, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of Mississippi, these characteristics can affect ordinary behaviors, including how people describe their own experiences.

According to recent reports, to investigate these connections, Drislane and Bray recruited 450 participants, including college students and individuals who reported having been incarcerated. Each person responded to open questions about important moments in their life, including their greatest highs, lowest points, and major turning points.

After writing their personal accounts, participants completed a questionnaire designed to measure their levels of psychopathic traits. The researchers then analyzed the written responses using specialized software that identifies patterns in word choice.

The analysis focused on how frequently participants used language associated with different psychological categories, including positive and negative emotions, achievement, social influence or clout, and risk. By comparing these language patterns with the personality scores, the team identified several intriguing relationships.

Surprising Differences in Positive and Negative Language.

Participants with higher disinhibition scores generally used more negative words in their personal stories. They were also less likely to mention friends or use language connected to positive emotions and personal achievement.

Meanness, however, showed a very different pattern. People scoring higher in this trait tended to use more positive language, along with more words related to achievement and rewards. They also used fewer expressions associated with negative emotions.

Sources indicate that boldness was associated with another distinctive pattern. Participants with higher scores used fewer anxiety-related words, including terms such as fear, afraid, and worry. Their personal accounts also contained fewer references to mental illness.

These differences suggest that psychopathic traits do not produce a single recognizable style of communication. Instead, different characteristics are associated with different ways of describing emotions, goals, relationships, and personal experiences.

Recent findings suggest that "What this tells us is the story we tell about our life has meaning," Drislane said. "It helps people make sense of their experiences, develop a worldview and a coherent sense of who they are.

"What we're starting to see is that in psychopathy, there are traits that relate to differences in meaning-making and the ways people think about their life.".

Why Psychopathy Is More Complex Than the Stereotypes.

The researchers also discovered that the relationship between personality traits and language changed depending on which question participants were answering. Someone describing a difficult experience, for example, might use language differently than when recalling a personal success.

This variation is important because it challenges the assumption that psychopathy is characterized by consistently flat or emotionally empty communication. Instead, the findings indicate that language patterns depend on both the particular psychopathic trait and the context in which someone is telling their story.

Sources indicate that "People tend to think of psychopathy as one thing, but it's actually multidimensional," Bray noted. "What we mean when we say that everyone exists on this spectrum. Everyone has some degree of meanness, boldness, and disinhibition.

It has been revealed that "Viewing it from a multidimensional perspective allows us to observe how those traits might manifest in nonforensic populations, in people who have not committed a crime. That allows us to see how these traits affect college students, business professionals, or interpersonal relationships.".

Industry observers note that like many personality conditions, psychopathy is better understood as a spectrum rather than a simple distinction between people who have it and those who do not. At one extreme is the familiar cultural image of a "psychopath," while people at the opposite end score low in all three dimensions.

In a recent development, this approach allows researchers to examine psychopathic traits throughout the general population, including among people who have never committed a crime. It also helps explain why the same broad label can encompass individuals with very different personalities and behaviors.

How Understanding Psychopathic Traits Could Improve Treatment.

Sources indicate that recognizing these differences has implications beyond understanding everyday speech. Researchers have linked dimensions of psychopathy to serious outcomes, including criminal behavior, repeat offending, and intimate partner violence. Examining each trait separately may provide a clearer picture of how these risks develop.

It has been revealed that "That's in part why there's a movement away from calling people 'psychopaths,' because we don't view psychopathy as a category," Drislane said. "But psychopathic dimensions can predict vital outcomes, things like crime, recidivism, or intimate partner violence.

"What our research, including this paper, suggests is that it's crucial to look beyond that label and into the different components or dimensions of psychopathy, because each of those dimensions actually has a unique set of outcomes or things that it can predict.".

Researchers also emphasize that psychopathy can be treated, with interventions aimed at reducing problematic symptoms and behaviors. Understanding the psychological processes behind boldness, meanness, and disinhibition could help scientists develop more targeted approaches and potentially identify ways to prevent severe problems from emerging.

In a recent development, "If we want to be able to treat or ideally even prevent psychopathy from developing, we need to understand the mechanisms at play," she noted. "That comes down to understanding the unique contributors for all three of these dimensions.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home Depot on Tuesday declared its chief financial officer, Richard McPhail, will become CEO of the company, succeeding Ted Decker, effective next week.

Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot stated Ann-Marie Campbell, currently senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to succeed McPhail.

Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The organization mentioned on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said.

According to recent reports, "I'm glad to be back and grateful for the support I received," Decker told analysts on Tuesday. "The board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession initiative.".

McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles.

"We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick.

He remarked the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using artificial intelligence tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market.

Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously remarked it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects.

Shares of Home Depot sank more than 3% following the announcement and the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results.

The CEO change came as the home improvement retailer posted quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations. The firm said comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount.

Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

According to recent reports, the company reported net income of $3.71 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.60 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86.

Revenue rose 4.9% compared with the year-ago period.

"We also are confident that we are taking material share from the market and from competition," McPhail said on the call with analysts.

In the third quarter, the company noted online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric.

The company said it saw positive comparable sales numbers in 13 out of 16 of its merchandising departments, including notable strength in the power department, which posted double-digit percentage growth.

For the full year, Home Depot noted it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase.

Home Depot added it expects adjusted earnings per share to rise 2% this year, compared with prior guidance of flat to a 4% increase.

Recent findings suggest that NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration.

Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology.

NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19.

Recent findings suggest that “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” mentioned Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.”.

The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy.

Industry observers note that the competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing plan, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams.

In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each.

Recent findings suggest that the AMPERE Challenge is open for registration until Jan. 27, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST. The challenge supports the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket project, managed by NASA Glenn and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The project is funded by the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Yet2 administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate.

Children’s Health Defense, which was allowed back after misinformation ban, accuses tech organization of censorship.

An anti-vaccine group led for years by Robert F Kennedy Jr remarked Meta has “taken down” posts on its accounts, after a Guardian report found the group was sharing false and misleading information about vaccines.

The Guardian reported on Wednesday that Children’s Health Defense (CHD) had earlier this year been allowed back on Facebook and Instagram, four years after Meta removed it from Facebook and Instagram for repeatedly violating its misinformation policies.

CHD stated in posts on X that within hours of the Guardian’s article running, “ALL of our accounts have been targeted”. It accused Meta of censorship.

“Our posts are being taken down AGAIN simply for sharing the truth about vaccines and the experiences of families whose children were injured by vaccines,” CHD posted on Wednesday night, adding: “People have every right to discuss vaccine injuries and share their experiences without being silenced by big tech.”.

Meta and CHD did not immediately return emails seeking comment.

Among the content that was no longer up as of Wednesday evening was a video that the group had posted on Facebook that noted the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is “not so safe and effective”.

Another video no longer available had been titled “Vaccines: Your child could die”, and made the misleading claim that vaccines are deadly.

A third video that was no longer up said the HPV vaccines are “very dangerous”, have “caused hundreds, thousands of deaths”, and do not prevent cervical cancer.

All three posts had been visible on CHD accounts at the time the Guardian story was published on Wednesday.

CHD on Wednesday evening posted screenshots of two messages it received about Meta’s action. They indicated two posts had been removed because of false information about vaccines, and cited Meta’s community standards.

“We don’t allow people to show false information that leading health organizations say could contribute to people refusing vaccines,” the message said.

A review by the Guardian had found that Children’s Health Defense (CHD) has reopened or opened six accounts on Facebook and Instagram from May through September this year, at a time when measles has come roaring back in the United States. Health officials have reported 11 measles-associated deaths in the US this year, and the country this week lost its measles elimination status.

The CHD news comes after a Guardian investigation this month found health and vaccine misinformation was rampant on Facebook in a massive public group, Crunchy Moms, and that Facebook was recommending it to consumers despite apparent violations of its policies.

Industry observers note that crunchy Moms was started a few months after Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg last year announced a rollback of moderation and factchecking. Zuckerberg defended the move at the time by saying he wanted to restore “free expression on our platforms”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19).
  • Extensive security measures have already been revealed for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants.
  • The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Extensive security measures have already been revealed for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that led by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London.

Sources indicate that but what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic.

Recent findings suggest that "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal," he told DW. "There is no plan outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises.".

Nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

Industry observers note that this has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)?

It has been revealed that after the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, Merz noted: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear.".

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President Antonio Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate says a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under.

"Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations," Meister mentioned. "Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that.".

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator.

At the federal government's regular press briefing, he remarked: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week.

Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he mentioned: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations.".

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question.".

Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: Peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

Recent findings suggest that european supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the glitch is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest DeutschlandTrend survey on the matter, conducted or German public broadcaster ARD in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

Recent findings suggest that A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing matter in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

This article was originally written in German.

#35837. A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal upcoming physics

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1625 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal upcoming physics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover.
  • The mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
  • When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover. But before researchers can determine whether this subtle signal reveals something extraordinary about the cosmos, they must answer a crucial question: Is the effect actually coming from the universe, or could it be an illusion created by the telescopes observing it?

The mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang. This ancient light provides a remarkable snapshot of the "baby universe" as it existed nearly 13.8 billion years ago, allowing scientists to investigate conditions from the earliest stages of cosmic history.

When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space. As radiation scattered off free electrons during this transition, it acquired a small amount of linear polarization. Polarization describes the direction in which light's electric field oscillates, and a similar effect occurs when sunlight scatters through Earth's atmosphere.

Now, observations suggest that the polarization of this ancient radiation may have shifted slightly as the light traveled across the universe. This possible rotation, called cosmic birefringence, is especially intriguing because it could point to physical processes not explained by the Standard Model, the leading theory describing fundamental particles and their interactions. Confirming the effect might even provide latest insights into dark matter and dark energy (see Sidebar).

A Mysterious Cosmic Signal or a Telescope Error?

It has been revealed that there is a major obstacle to interpreting this potential discovery. An extremely small error in how a telescope's polarization detectors are aligned can produce a signal that looks almost identical to cosmic birefringence.

To help address this problem, physicists at the University of California San Diego developed a latest technique for checking how accurately different groups of detectors measure polarization angles. They tested their approach using existing observations collected by the European Space Agency's Planck satellite, which mapped the universe's ancient radiation in extraordinary detail.

It has been revealed that the research was led by Postdoctoral Fellow Anto I. Lonappan, Chancellor's Distinguished Professor of Physics Brian Keating, and Associate Professor of Physics Kam Arnold. Their findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Separating Real Cosmic Effects From Instrument Errors.

Previous studies have suggested that the polarization of the CMB may have rotated by just a fraction of a degree over its nearly 14 billion years of travel. Although that sounds insignificant, such a tiny change could have enormous implications for fundamental physics.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, a telescope whose polarization detectors are misaligned by a similarly small angle could produce precisely the same apparent rotation. If every detector shares the same alignment error, the resulting measurements cannot distinguish that error from a genuine rotation of the cosmic signal.

In a recent development, the UC San Diego researchers found a way to investigate the problem from another angle. Rather than relying on a single combined measurement, they compared separate polarization maps generated by different groups of detectors.

If cosmic birefringence is real, its effect should appear consistently across all these maps. By comparing the maps with one another, the researchers can effectively eliminate any rotation shared by all of them. What remains reveals differences in the calibration of the individual detector groups, making it possible to identify inconsistencies that might otherwise complicate the search for new physics.

Recent findings suggest that "The signal we are looking for is incredibly small, so we have to be certain that we are seeing the universe and not our instrument," said Lonappan. "Our method gives us a complementary way to check that distinction. Before interpreting a tiny rotation as fresh physics, we want to know that the calibration itself can be trusted.".

Testing the Mystery With Planck Satellite Data.

To evaluate their technique, the researchers analyzed eight polarization maps produced using Planck observations. They then compared their findings with results from an established approach called the Minami-Komatsu analysis, which is used to distinguish instrumental rotation from possible cosmic birefringence.

It has been revealed that although the two methods rely on different assumptions, they produced consistent results. This agreement provides an important independent check on how relative detector calibration errors are being assessed.

In a recent development, the new approach also has a deliberate limitation. Because it removes any rotation common to all the maps, it cannot independently measure the overall polarization angle or determine how much the universe itself may have rotated the light. Establishing that absolute rotation still requires an independent reference for calibrating the overall angle.

Industry observers note that to demonstrate how their findings fit with existing measurements, the researchers combined their reconstruction of relative calibration differences with the common calibration value inferred from the established analysis. This produced an estimated cosmic birefringence angle of 0.37 ± 0.12 degrees, matching the Minami-Komatsu result.

According to recent reports, importantly, this agreement does not independently confirm that the ancient light has actually rotated. Instead, it shows that the newly introduced method can reproduce results from the existing framework while providing a separate way to examine potential calibration problems.

Searching for Gravitational Waves From the Early Universe.

The technique could also play an crucial role in another major pursuit in cosmology: the search for gravitational waves generated during the universe's earliest moments.

To understand why, scientists distinguish between two patterns of polarization in the cosmic microwave background, known as E modes and B modes.

E modes were first detected in 2002. They arise from density variations in the early universe and form symmetric polarization patterns. B modes have a different appearance, featuring patterns that resemble curls or swirls.

One known source of B modes is gravitational lensing, which occurs when the gravity of matter between Earth and the early universe bends and distorts the path of ancient light. Scientists have already observed B modes created through this process.

Recent findings suggest that however, researchers are also searching for a different kind of B mode that could have been produced by primordial gravitational waves. These ripples in spacetime may have originated during an extremely early period of rapid cosmic expansion, known as inflation. The distinctive B mode signal associated with those primordial gravitational waves has not yet been detected.

Finding it would provide powerful evidence about gravitational waves in the early universe and could offer strong support for particular models of cosmic inflation, potentially transforming scientists' understanding of how the universe began.

Why Extremely Precise Measurements Matter.

According to recent reports, the challenge is that even a slight error in a telescope's polarization calibration can cause some of the much stronger E-mode signal to appear incorrectly as B modes. This contamination could make an instrumental artifact look like an exciting cosmological discovery.

Industry observers note that the UC San Diego method could help prevent such mistakes by identifying differences in polarization angle calibration among detector groups. That makes it a potentially valuable tool for future experiments searching for the extremely faint signatures of primordial gravitational waves.

Industry observers note that this kind of independent verification will become increasingly crucial as observatories develop the ability to measure cosmic polarization with greater precision. One example is the Simons Observatory, where Keating serves as principal investigator.

As these instruments become more sensitive, researchers will need equally rigorous methods for confirming that the faint signals they detect are genuine features of the universe rather than imperfections in their equipment.

"The detection of primordial B modes would transform our understanding of the early universe, so the measurement must survive rigorous calibration checks," stated Keating. "Anto has developed a useful newly introduced framework for testing relative polarization-angle calibration. This is ultimately about knowing when we can trust a measurement.".

Beyond the Standard Model: Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

The possibility of cosmic birefringence is particularly fascinating because it could reveal physics that lies beyond the Standard Model.

Although this framework has been remarkably successful at describing fundamental particles and their interactions, it cannot explain everything in the universe. Among its most important unanswered questions are the identity of dark matter and the origin and observed magnitude of dark energy. Together, these mysterious components account for approximately 95% of the universe's total energy density.

One possible explanation for cosmic birefringence involves a hypothetical field associated with particles resembling axions. Such a field could interact with light and gradually alter its polarization as it crosses the universe. However, these particles have not been confirmed to exist, and they would not necessarily be responsible for dark matter.

Other theoretical explanations connect the possible rotation to fields associated with dark energy, the mysterious phenomenon linked to the accelerating expansion of the universe.

If cosmic birefringence is eventually confirmed, it could provide an entirely newly introduced way to investigate these cosmic mysteries and reveal evidence of physical laws beyond those presently understood.

Recent findings suggest that for now, the first challenge is ensuring that the subtle signal can be trusted. By giving researchers another way to identify potential measurement errors, the upcoming technique strengthens the foundation for future discoveries that could reshape our picture of the universe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holidays are often a fun break during a busy year – a long weekend here and there is an event many of us can get behind. However, when a short holiday break turns into a full holiday season, we know that this is a different “ball game”.

In a recent development, everyone has stress about something – some people love the holidays, and some people are holiday-avoidant… and some live in the middle. What specific stressors or challenges you experience might not bother your sibling, your spouse or your coworker. We want to be aware of and have a clear understanding of what holidays mean to you as a person.

The first step is to acknowledge what your feelings and emotions are – you may enjoy seeing the neighborhood holiday lights but not want to decorate yourself (totally okay!!), you may love shopping for the perfect gift for everyone on your list, you may avoid all of the activities — everyone one of these is an okay choice… you can be yourself always in all ways. Give yourself that permission. As you prepare, keep a list or a calendar of events – expected/obligated, okay to go or not go,.

Combine this with your standard calendar and make a schedule. If you want, add to the list what your part is (bring a dish, gift, coordinate a visit, etc.). Having the majority of activities written down will help you not overbook, help you proposal ahead, make it easier to say no, spend within your budget. Before you commit to something, say “I have to check my calendar first…. I will get back to you”.

Prepare your budget – We often budget for gifts but forget that we will be buying more groceries for those special meals and favorite dishes…. We also need to budget for travel, having guests in your home, clothing, even allow for a higher electric bill. Write it down – keep receipts – let your immediate family know that this is what we have to spend, then track it as you go.

Now that you have a current calendar and a working budget, set realistic expectations for your holiday experience. We know that not everything is optional and traditions will continue but none of it has to be perfect…minor stress and family friction can be normal.

Industry observers note that when telling someone no, use “I” statements and stick to the single issue at hand. In addition to your list/calendar, remember to prioritize time for yourself. Keep your regular sleep schedule as much as possible, eat well (if you have a heavy meal one day, lighten up the next), schedule time to get fresh air and a quick break. ALWAYS focus on what matters. Focus on meaningful connections rather than activities that cause you anxiety.

Sources indicate that if you feel emotional, take a few moments alone and identify the feeling, honor yourself for being able to face it and breathe through it (avoid pushing it down). Remember how many times you have gotten through a “pressure moment” and give yourself credit. Call a trusted friend or your therapist if you feel overwhelmed for longer than a day….and, please call 988 if you feel overwhelmed to an extreme. 988 is always available and waiting to help.

Look for the glimmers – find a happy moment (no matter how brief), find the memories that make you smile. Thinking of something joyful changes your emotional state… train yourself to do this any time you need a lift. Ultimately, we want to move away from focusing on the future (It causes anxiety) or overthinking about the past (it causes depression) ….and find yourself in the here and now where you have power to manage things happening around you. Your power is with you in the present. (Eckert Tolle book – The Power of Now).

The holiday season lasts for weeks – gift yourself with.

In a recent development, person sitting on sofa next to a holiday tree. With the extra pressure of the holiday season, our feelings can often be stronger than other times during the year…. if you start having feelings: Anxious – take deep breaths, focus ONLY on the present – your surroundings, what you see, count objects, put ice on the inside of your wrists (this works really well!) Angry – walk away for a moment, take a break, give yourself as long as you need to regulate these feelings, know that whoever gets angry first loses…be the winner in the moment. Helpless, hopeless, trapped (discouraged) – remember that you have a voice, it is sometimes difficult to use it in family situations, but you can talk to yourself. Remember how strong you are, how many accomplishments you have completed…. reframe the situation so you recall all of your wonderful qualities. Overwhelmed – Check your list/holiday calendar again…what can you change or take off the list. What can you postpone for 24-48 hours? What can you give someone else to do? What can you order from the store rather than do the cooking or shopping yourself? Find a quick solution for one or two things (at least) and take some pressure off. Grief – acknowledge how you feel, we do not have to be cheerful just because it is a holiday. Say no to any event or activity that feels too “heavy” and give yourself permission to leave if it becomes too much. Find a way to keep their memory with you – carry a favorite picture or memento. Find a grief support group. Basically, we want to notice the small things and find gratitude in what we have. Our outward situation does not define us. If you find that holiday time is difficult or stressful, always give yourself permission to contact your EAP services for assistance and support.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

Sources indicate that the annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Recent findings suggest that leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

Recent findings suggest that but back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows.".

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026.

It has been revealed that this phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively quickly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, Newly introduced Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

Recent findings suggest that "But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog.".

Recent findings suggest that but the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

"One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Sources indicate that elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

If the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Wife of Trump ally Todd Blanche promoted treatments with unproven medical claims

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kristine Blanche, named to US health advisory role, offered purported treatments for Epstein-Barr virus and HPV.
  • Attorney general Todd Blanche’s wife, Kristine Blanche, who was appointed earlier this year to a US government advisory board on alternative medicine, has a website on which she marketed dietary supplements and treatments with unproven medical and health claims.
  • Blanche is a licensed physician assistant who says she has a PhD in breast thermography from the University of Science, Arts and Technology in Montserrat, a British territory in the Caribbean.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kristine Blanche, named to US health advisory role, offered purported treatments for Epstein-Barr virus and HPV.

Attorney general Todd Blanche’s wife, Kristine Blanche, who was appointed earlier this year to a US government advisory board on alternative medicine, has a website on which she marketed dietary supplements and treatments with unproven medical and health claims.

Blanche is a licensed physician assistant who says she has a PhD in breast thermography from the University of Science, Arts and Technology in Montserrat, a British territory in the Caribbean. She is also an advocate for alternative medical cures and holistic health.

Her site also links to a page called “Dr Blanche’s Dispensary”, where patients can buy supplement pills she recommends. She suggested that one product, a liquid herbal compound, could be used to treat the Epstein-Barr virus, although she misspelled “Epstein”.

There is no medication approved by the FDA to treat or cure Epstein-Barr, and the product itself does not claim to treat the virus.

Blanche also listed five supplements in her store, priced up to $63 a bottle, which she mentioned can help treat human papillomavirus (HPV).

Another treatment Blanche offers, priced online at $595, claims to help men “boost” their testosterone levels and lose weight.

The day after the Guardian emailed questions to Blanche about the supplements she offered, the products related to purported treatments for Epstein-Barr and HPV disappeared from her website. Her online store carries a disclaimer that “these statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. These products are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.”.

In a recent development, peter Lurie, the executive director of the Center for Science in the Public Interest, noted that Blanche’s website highlights gaps in regulations of claims made by providers. “That leaves an opening for some to exploit,” he said. “It is not in the interest of American patients, but it is not clearly illegal.”.

It has been revealed that blanche wrote to the Guardian that she has “a PhD and an MD degree”, and mentioned she complies “with all mandatory FDA guidelines. Any publication to the contrary is false and defamatory.”.

She remarked that while she has a medical degree from the university in Montserrat, she has never been a licensed physician in the US. She has previously practiced as a physician assistant.

In April, Blanche was appointed to the advisory council of the federal National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH). The center, which has a $170m annual budget, supports research on alternative and holistic medicines and practices.

“It absolutely concerns me,” Lurie said of her appointment. “I have no confidence that the attorney general’s wife, with a financial interest in the kind of products this advisory committee concerns itself with, would be appropriate on the committee.”.

In response to questions, a National Institutes of Health (NIH) spokesperson emailed that “the Trump administration is bringing the best and brightest into HHS”, adding: “Dr Kristine Blanche was appointed through the established appointment process based on her work and background in integrative health. Her experience provides a relevant foundation for service and a valuable perspective to inform the council’s work, in compliance with the charter.”.

Recent findings suggest that iris International, which invests in medical companies, also hired Blanche this year as its chief medical officer. A spokesperson for the manufacturer wrote that Blanche “reports to the CEO and provides a view on emerging healthcare businesses in the market”.

It is unclear how much business Blanche does on her website, which appears to have been active for over a decade.

In Todd Blanche’s 2025 and 2026 financial disclosures, his wife’s income from “Integrative Healing Center” is not large, listed at just between $1,000 and $15,000.

Her “Man Up” cleanse and “Girlfriend” cleanse – each priced at almost $600 – are still available, and include detoxes, shakes, videos and dietary supplements.

Recent findings suggest that “Lose weight, boost your testosterone & ditch the toxins. All while eating real food,” the Man Up program promises.

Sources indicate that “I’m going to share with you how you can turn back your body into that place it was before. I’ve had patients lose 40 pounds,” Blanche remarked in a video sales pitch on YouTube. “It’s not acceptable to you if you’re not really feeling great.”.

She has praised the use of a type of alternative diagnostic imaging technology called “thermography” – which detects heat variations in the body – and in a podcast has remarked it can predict potential risks years before mammograms. Her website indicates her PhD thesis was about “breast thermography”.

The FDA has approved the use of thermography if it is used with mammography, but has warned it cannot be a substitute.

It has been revealed that the Blanches moved to Florida in 2024 and the website notes she has a virtual practice in Palm Beach Gardens, where the couple live, not far from Mar-a-Lago. Her PA license lists her home address.

Last month, Blanche appeared on a little-watched podcast called I Choose Health, run by Stefan Lessie, a Newly introduced York City-based personal trainer who posts inspirational and educational interviews with doctors and health activists.

Sources indicate that lessie has a tiny audience of about 20 to 30 listeners a week on Spotify. He said he received an unsolicited email last month from a PR executive explaining that “my client Kristine Blanche would resonate with your audience”.

It has been revealed that lessie interviewed Blanche for an hour, as she discussed her practice and her philosophy of medicine. “A lot of women come to me after they’ve been to many doctors over several years of suffering,” she told him.

In a recent development, “I love that the Maha movement is out there,” Blanche said, referring to Robert F Kennedy Jr’s Make America Healthy Again movement. “Trying to educate moms on, you know, food dyes are bad.”.

Sources indicate that lessie remarked he did not know who Blanche was. “I was doing some research after the interview, and I saw her husband, and I was like: ‘He’s the US attorney general!’ And I was like, ‘Wow!’”.

Blanche has received little, if any, public attention. A Stat News article in April reported her appointment to the federal advisory council.

The former head of the NCCIH, Dr Helene Langevin, a professor at the University of Vermont, said the advisory council role is “crucial” because members review every research grant decision made by independent panels.

Langevin, who retired in September 2025, declined to discuss specifics about Blanche. “I can’t comment on the qualifications of any advisory board member,” she remarked.

NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange new world

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising upcoming perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.
  • Industry observers note that on September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system.
  • It has been revealed that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising upcoming perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.

Industry observers note that on September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system. Hera's latest image provides a look at its larger companion, Didymos, from a side that scientists had not previously seen in such detail.

It has been revealed that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white. Although most of Dimorphos, which measures 151 m across, is concealed in shadow, the much larger Didymos, with a diameter of 780 m, is clearly visible.

A Surprisingly Different Side of Asteroid Didymos.

Industry observers note that "The first thing we noted was wow!" observes Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur. "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART's camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole new world.

"This side of Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator that we saw before, but otherwise appears very different, with multiple boulders and craters and what look like patterns of grooves or ridges.".

The newly revealed terrain raises intriguing questions about how the asteroid's surface developed and whether NASA's collision with Dimorphos may have left traces on its larger neighbor.

According to recent reports, when DART struck Dimorphos, the impact sent material flying into space. Scientists believe some of that debris may have traveled across the roughly 1 km separating the two asteroids and reached Didymos. Determining whether this material contributed to the features now visible on its surface will be an key part of Hera's investigation.

ESA's Hera mission scientist Michael Kueppers adds: "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 km of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out. We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify.".

NASA's DART Mission Changed an Asteroid's Orbit.

Sources indicate that although Dimorphos is largely obscured in Hera's upcoming image, it holds a remarkable place in space exploration history. It became the first object in the Solar System to have its orbit measurably altered by human activity.

It has been revealed that NASA achieved this milestone by sending the 580 kg DART spacecraft into Dimorphos at approximately 6.1 km/s. The collision reduced the time the smaller asteroid takes to complete an orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, give or take a minute. That change was substantially greater than scientists had anticipated.

The experiment demonstrated that striking an asteroid with a spacecraft can change its motion through space. This approach, known as kinetic impact deflection, could potentially be used to redirect a dangerous asteroid before it reaches Earth.

Hera Begins Its Investigation of NASA's Asteroid Impact.

It has been revealed that after a two-year journey, Hera has reached the double asteroid system, located 196.8 million km from Earth. The spacecraft is now preparing for a detailed 'crash site investigation' to examine the consequences of NASA's groundbreaking experiment.

While DART demonstrated that an asteroid's orbit could be changed through a deliberate collision, Hera will help scientists understand the physical processes behind the result. By examining both asteroids and documenting their characteristics, researchers hope to improve their ability to predict how future asteroid deflection attempts might work.

Recent findings suggest that the findings could help transform kinetic impact deflection from a successful one-time demonstration into a dependable, repeatable planetary defense technique. Such a capability could prove critical if an asteroid were ever discovered on a collision course with Earth.

In a recent development, "Seeing this image is a hugely exciting moment for the whole Hera family," comments Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli. "It has taken years of hard work and dedication to reach this point - but we're motivated to know that the adventure is only beginning!".

The mission's next major reveal is scheduled for November 25, when detailed images of both Didymos and Dimorphos will be unveiled, giving scientists and the public a closer look at the asteroids involved in humanity's first successful asteroid deflection experiment.
